title: Prefetch selector constraints - arch review notes
content:
Context:
This meeting captured the architectural review of the Prefetch Selector Constraints RFC — an effort to formalize which requests we prefetch into the KV/prefix cache and under what constraints (cost budget, tenant fairness, model-seq-length heuristics, and eviction pressure). The goal is to reduce cold-start token cost by warming frequently reused prefixes without harming latency SLOs or incurring disproportionate GPU memory pressure across tenants.

Attendees:
- Aisha Patel (owner)
- Miguel Torres
- Kai Huang
- Rina Bose
- Evan Cole
- Notes: recorded in meeting audio; summary below.

Agenda:
1) Quick recap of RFC goals and current prototype behavior
2) Selector constraint primitives: budget, score threshold, per-tenant caps
3) Interaction with autoscaling & burst capacity
4) Failure and fallback modes (eviction storms, noisy tenants)
5) Telemetry & rollout plan
6) Open questions and action items

Summary of current prototype:
- Prototype selects candidate prefixes from recent traffic by computing a simple reuse-score = frequency * (1 - avg_seq_length/128).
- Prefetch queue drains at a fixed token budget per-second per-host, shared across tenants with a naive weighting by qps.
- Early experiments in staging showed 12-18% per-token latency reduction for warmed prefixes, but also occasional memory spikes when multiple tenants had correlated hot prefixes.

Key design discussion points and decisions:
1) Constraint primitives to adopt (DECISION):
   - Keep three orthogonal constraints: global token budget (host-level), per-tenant token cap, and dynamic score threshold.
   - Default values: global budget = 20K tokens/s per-GPU host (tunable), tenant cap = 25% of host budget, score threshold adaptive based on tail-latency signal.
   - Rationale: global safeguard prevents runaway prefetching under misconfigured workloads; tenant cap enforces fairness for multi-tenant hosts; adaptive threshold reduces wasted prefetch on noisy short sequences.

2) Scoring function revision (DECISION):
   - Replace linear (frequency * length penalty) with a decayed exponential score: score = freq * exp(-alpha * avg_seq_len) * recency_boost where alpha = 0.01 by default.
   - Weight recency with an LRU-ish time decay (half-life ~ 5 minutes). Reason: more robust to bursty spikes and better favors prefixes reused across minutes.

3) Prefetch batching & eviction interaction (DECISION):
   - Prefetch should allocate entries into a soft-reserved partition of the KV hotset. When soft partition exceeds 60% of host memory pressure threshold, new prefetches are paused until pressure drops.
   - Eviction policy for prefetch entries: use a two-tier LRU with score-aware demotion. High-score prefetch entries can survive eviction longer.

4) Noisy-tenant mitigation (DECISION):
   - Introduce a noisy-tenant circuit breaker: if a tenant's prefetch hit-rate falls below 5% over a 10-minute window while consuming > 10% of prefetch budget, throttle that tenant to 10% of previous cap for 15 minutes and surface alert to on-call.

5) Autoscaler & burst capacity integration (DECISION):
   - During autoscale-up or burst-capacity events we allow temporary increase of global prefetch budget up to 2x to speed warmup, but requires a rollback timer (10m) and must respect per-tenant hard caps.

6) Fallback modes (DECISION):
   - If KV hotset memory crosses 85% of the host limit, immediately pause prefetch producers, mark the host as "prefetch_disabled" in routing metadata, and fail-open requests to non-prefetch variant.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: correlated warmups saturate host memory leading to evictions of active conversation state. Mitigation: soft partition + 85% hard stop + eviction demotion policy.
- Risk: per-tenant caps too tight reduce benefits for bursty tenants. Mitigation: autoscale-aware temporary budget expansion and metrics-driven tuning.
- Risk: complexity in scoring parameters (alpha, half-life). Mitigation: expose as flags and run controlled experiments to sweep a small grid; default conservative values ship first.

Telemetry & SLOs to track:
- Prefetch hit-rate (per-host, per-tenant)
- Tokens prefetched/sec (global and per-tenant)
- Memory usage of KV hotset and partition sizes
- Tail GPU latency (P95/P99) correlated with prefetch activity
- Eviction rate and new-prefetch pause events
- Noisy-tenant throttles triggered and duration
- Experiment metric: delta in per-token cost (micro-billed) and tail-latency for warmed vs non-warmed requests

Experiment plan (A/B ramp):
Phase 0 (canary, 1 host): enable prefetch-producer with global budget=5K tokens/s, tenant cap=40% for low-risk tenant, run 48 hours, validate no memory regressions.
Phase 1 (small cohort, 5 hosts): enable scoring function + soft partition, budget=10K tokens/s, collect hit-rate and tail-latency for 7 days.
Phase 2 (scaled, 25 hosts): enable noisy-tenant protection and autoscale-burst allowance, budget=20K tokens/s, run 2 weeks, evaluate cost delta and SLO impact.
Rollout gated on: no increase in P99 > 5% from baseline, acceptable memory headroom (>15% free), and prefetched-token cost per successful hit < 0.3x of equivalent non-prefetch token cost savings.

Operational runbook snippets (short):
- If host memory > 85%: control plane flag sets host to prefetch_disabled; on-call to investigate recent tenant prefetch patterns and consider temporary tenant caps; consider draining prefetch queue.
- If noisy-tenant throttle fires > 3 times in 24h: SE team to contact tenant and consider dedicated placement or reserved capacity.

Open questions (to resolve before finalizing RFC):
- Should we allow model-specific weighting in score function (e.g., smaller models are cheaper to prefetch)? (action: Kai to prototype model-cost multiplier by 2025-01-21)
- Revisit per-tenant cap default: 25% vs 40% tradeoffs — need small cohort experiment. (action: Miguel to run parameter sweep in staging)
- Do we want to expose a developer-level opt-out API for customers that cannot tolerate any prefetching of their prefixes? (action: Rina to draft API and privacy implications by 2025-01-24)

Action items (owner -- due):
- Kai Huang -- prototype model-cost multiplier and report simple cost model (2025-01-21)
- Miguel Torres -- run tenant cap sweep in staging and produce recommended default (2025-01-23)
- Rina Bose -- draft customer opt-out API and privacy/spec implications (2025-01-24)
- Evan Cole -- add prefetched-token telemetry to runtime metrics pipeline (dashboard + alert) (2025-01-22)
- Aisha Patel -- update RFC with agreed constraint primitives and scoring function, push RFC v2 (2025-01-18)

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus review on: eviction interaction and noisy-tenant safeguards. These are intentionally conservative; tradeoffs are spelled out in the rollout plan.
- If you have dataset traces that show correlated hot-prefix patterns across tenants, please drop them in the linked PR or ping Aisha directly so we can simulate stress cases.

Appendix (quick math):
- Example: host budget 20K tokens/s, tenant cap 25% => tenant max 5K tokens/s. If average warm prefix length is 32 tokens and 60% of prefetched prefixes see at least one hit within 30s, the effective warmed-token savings approximates: saved_tokens/s ~= hit_rate * prefetched_tokens/s * (avg_warm_len - avg_overlap). Plugging conservative numbers yields ~3K saved tokens/s which is materially positive for high-cost GPU models.

Meeting adjourned. Next sync: 2025-01-21 10:00am PT (follow-up on action items and first-stage canary results).
